top_story.headline: No new FEC compliance filings surfaced since the last edition
top_story.dek: All 43 RFAI and Form 99 filings in the 3-day window were already reported in earlier editions.
paragraphs: The window covers filings received October 30 onward. Forty-three RFAI and Form 99 filings fall inside it, and every one has already appeared in a prior edition, so none is repeated here.
The input also contains no new voided or negative transactions of $10,000 or more and no red-flag keyword hits.

sections.headline: $120,000 in new independent expenditures
paragraphs: 1 new independent expenditures of $50K or more, $120,000 in all. Largest target: Mary Peltola (support, $120,000). 1 spender(s) registered in the last 180 days.

blocks.text: Independent expenditures of $50K+ reported since 10/30/2026 (24/48-hour notices plus regular reports), counting only items not shown in an earlier edition. A shared vendor is a coordination-risk flag, not proof: FEC rules allow common vendors behind a firewall. Generic platforms (ActBlue, Google, postal, banks, broadcasters) are excluded.

footer.coverage_window: FEC RFAI (FRQ) and Form 99 filings received October 30, 2026 through November 2, 2026 (PM edition), excluding filings reported in earlier editions.
footer.sources: FEC filings API; FEC Schedule A/B itemized transactions.

apod.title: A Long Cloud on Mars
apod.caption: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft.
